reuse.why: The change reuses getRangedAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, but getScheduledAmount only partially delegates to the new expected-amount abstraction.

duplication.why: Most consumer-side calculations are consolidated, but missing-value and number-versus-range dispatch remain duplicated between getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, tolerance stays in shared/rules, and API serialization stays in api-models.

scope.why: The edits are confined to schedule amount policy, its consumers, API exposure, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Two overlapping amount helpers and an optional third-position operator leave maintainers managing separate dispatch paths and inconsistent operator propagation among existing consumers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getScheduledAmount handles missing and ranged amounts directly rather than delegating all expected-amount selection to getExpectedAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining dispatch duplication is explicit; the diff otherwise replaces local calculations with shared helper calls.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter after inverse, while getExpectedAmount introduces the isapprox branch; getScheduledAmount bypasses that unified dispatcher for missing and ranged amounts, and existing callers continue omitting the operator.
